title: Desktop app with an installer
fits: A program people download and run on their own Windows, Mac or Linux computer, updated from GitHub releases.
notFor: a very small download or very low memory use (each app carries its own browser engine)

stack.choice: Electron 45 with Electron Forge 8 and Vite
stack.why: The official way to build, package and publish an Electron app; one code base for all three systems.
Types catch mistakes between the window and the main process.

stack.choice: Vitest for logic, Playwright for driving the real app
stack.why: Playwright can start and click through an Electron app.

stack.choice: Forge makers (Windows installer, zip, Linux packages) and GitHub releases

after.do: Set productName, description and author in package.json to the app's real details (the setup tool fills in this computer's user name, which would ship inside the app).

host.name: GitHub releases
host.deploy: npm run make builds the installers; npm run publish with @electron-forge/publisher-github uploads them to a draft release. Set up by /starter-kit:launch; not part of the recipe test.

accounts.name: GitHub
accounts.why: Holds the code, runs the checks and hosts the downloads.

accounts.name: A Windows code-signing certificate
accounts.why: Without it Windows shows an 'unknown publisher' warning on install.

accounts.name: An Apple Developer account
accounts.when: only if it ships for Mac
accounts.why: Mac apps must be signed and notarized to open without a warning.

settings.name: GITHUB_TOKEN
settings.why: Only on the machine or GitHub job that publishes releases; never in the app.

notes: Three parts with different powers: src/main.ts (full computer access), src/preload.ts (the only bridge), src/renderer.ts (the window, a web page with no Node access). Keep it that way.
Expose to the window only named functions through contextBridge in the preload, each doing one checked thing. Never expose ipcRenderer itself, fs, or a 'run any command' function.
Never turn on nodeIntegration or turn off contextIsolation or sandbox, and never load remote web pages into a window that has the preload.
Open outside links in the user's browser (shell.openExternal on an allow-listed address), never inside the app window.
The fuses in forge.config.mts are security settings (RunAsNode off, asar integrity on): don't loosen them.
This is Forge 8: config is forge.config.mts and the build output is .vite/build/main.cjs. Check node_modules/@electron-forge/cli/README.md before using an option you remember from older Forge.
Save the user's data under app.getPath('userData'), never next to the program (that folder is read-only once installed).
Lint and formatting are oxlint and oxfmt, not ESLint and Prettier: npm run lint:fix fixes most findings.
